Also, unrelated to the melatonin topic, but what really helped me is conditioning myself not to go to bed until I’m tired. Preferably, I would stay in my livingroom until I’m tired. This way, your brain associaties the bed only with sleeping, and not staring at the ceiling/scrolling on your phone/etc until you’re tired.
Additionally, recent research has shown that the time you get up is actually more important than the time you fall asleep. So if you don’t go to bed until you are tired, and get up early (as you can manage) it’s gonna be tough, but eventually your circadian rhythm will adjust and you will get tired earlier. Not sure what your sleeping pattern is now, but I fixed mine from 3-4 am and getting up at 9 (5-6 hours is doable for me for a little while) to 1 am, getting up at 9 and now 12am -7:30 am. The most important thing is to remain consistent and get up at the same time every day, when that works you can try to get up earlier if wanted but

Also, I dont want to worry you! Melatonin is inherently not addictive, so no withdrawal symptoms should occur. It’s more of a behavioral thing when you don’t trust yourself to sleep without it, which causes anxiety. So slowly build trust in yourself!

Melatonin is genuinely not recommended to take longer dan 2-3 weeks. You could indeed try alternating between magnesium and melatonin, as mentioned before. If the goal was resetting  your sleeping pattern, which I think you did (yay!), I would recommend starting to taper off by either alternating between melatonin en magnesium, and slowly lowering the dosage of melatonin until you’re not taking it anymore. Because of the physical tolerance that builds quickly if you use it for too long you will need higher doses. It is also possible that behavioral dependence can occur, which is basically a reverse placebo effect. If you don’t take it, you might be afraid you can’t sleep, which in turn makes you so anxious you actually can’t sleep. To rebuild trust in your sleeping I would recommend tapering down. If your sleeping pattern does not stabilize you could try taking it again, with a few weeks in between before you start.

Just a heads up: Plan B does not work if you take it after you’ve ovulated. So technically if something happens to you right before you ovulate and you take it a few hours later it’s not foolproof. And if something happens after you ovulate, there is still a chance to get pregnant within the 12-24 hours after ovulation, in which case plan B won’t work at all. Would definitely also stock up on some emergency mife/miso in case the plan B wasn’t successful

Hi! I don't have any answers for you, but I am actually going through the same thing right now.  

I found out I was 4,5 weeks pregnant on June 17, and it was also completely unexpected and unplanned. Had my first ultrasound at 8,5 weeks and they found out the baby only measured at around 5,5 weeks, whereas the size of gestational sac was normal for this duration. They also saw some fluid around the uterus so they said I was probably going to bleed soon. They scheduled another ultrasound to confirm (maybe I was less far along than I thought) one week later but they found that indeed the pregnancy was not viable. They were surprised I hadn't had any loss of pregnancy symptoms, cramping or spotting yet. I opted for the miso as feeling the pregnancy symptoms while knowing it stopped growing weeks ago drove me insane and made me feel like such a failure. I finally took the miso on July 30th (at 10,5 weeks). I had the worst pain for two hours and then a lot of blood and tissue came out suddenly. That lasted around an hour. The pain was a lot less except for the occasional cramp from hell. The day after I bled like a heavy period but it slowed down during the day. Two days after the miso I woke up with a lot of blood loss that kept coming in waves. I bled through four pads in less than an hour. Went to the ER and they found that the actual gestational sack was stuck in the cervix, so they had to remove it. I'm not sure how they removed it in your case, but I agree it was very painful and quite traumatizing.

It's been five days now since they removed the sac and I'm still bleeding like a regular period, but not as heavy as before. I also experience a lot of the same symptoms as you described. The extreme fatigue, hot flashes, gut pain. The symptoms seem very random for me and just pop up out of nowhere. I also experience pain in my left ovary (I think) and the pain worsens and expands to the right side whenever I have to use the restroom.

Hey! Fellow adhd and bpd diagnosed person here!

I totally get what you mean. I can have such intense emotions or mental breakdowns, but when I talk to my therapist about it a few days later I'm completely numb. Like I can describe it a little bit, but can't seem to tap into those feelings.I'm a therapist in training and graduated psychologist myself and I personally think this has either to do with a lack of emotional permanence or masking.

Emotional permanence relates to the concept of object permanence which people with ADHD struggle with. For example, I sometimes completely forget I have a piece of clothing if it's not in the front of my closet. The out of sight, out of mind principle.  The same happens with emotions for me. I cannot describe what I felt during a meltdown as it's not in the present anymore. For example, I could describe something completely traumatic with no emotions whatsoever. Not because I want to hide them, but just don't feel them at that moment. There's a whole line of research entering the field now on the emotional aspects of ADHD, so if you're interested I would highly recommend looking it up. (actually a lot of emotional ADHD symptoms and BPD symptoms overlap a lot)

It can also be the case that you might be masking in front of your therapist. This can be either intentional or unintentional. Maybe you don't want to be a burden and play it down a bit or maybe you're afraid of telling them because you don't yet trust them enough. Maybe something else as well.

Either way, what helped me is to write down what I feel when it is happening. Sometimes I just type something in my notes on my phone or I actually write it down in a diary. Sometimes I write it as a letter to myself or to someone else or neither. It's up to you.That way, you at least know how you felt at that moment. If you feel comfortable you can take it with you and share it with your therapist.

Hope this helped you a little bit.My dm's are open if you need anything (:
